properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22: "if reflow2 isn't doing it for itself, then how can I assume it isn't doing it for other reflow2 designs?"

⭐ THIS IS THE DEEPEST OF THE FOUR AND THE ONE WITH NO EXISTING MECHANISM. The other questions ask how to make reflow2 close its own loop. This one asks whether reflow2 can SEE that a loop was never closed — in any design, including somebody else's — and today the answer is no. There is no reading anywhere that says "no test result has ever been fed into this design". 311 passing checks and 0 that ever failed look identical to a perfectly healthy project and to one that has never once reported a failure.

🛑 AND IT IS THE SAME CLASS THE DESIGN ALREADY NAMES ABOUT ITSELF, at the highest level yet: a detector reporting zero because it had NOTHING TO RUN ON reads exactly like one that ran clean. `loop_status` already refuses an unknown contributor id for this reason. The loop-closure question is that rule applied to the loop itself, and it has never been asked.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OTHER THREE: reflow2's whole claim is that a design stays true to what is fielded. A consumer cannot check that claim today. They get the same toolkit this repository got — complete, opt-in, undriven — and a design that reads verified because somebody typed it. If the loop is never closed, reflow2 degrades into a very well-organised wish list, and nothing in the product says so.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) A LOOP-CLOSURE READING, computed and never stored: how many checks have EVER been reconciled against a real run; when the last reconcile happened; how many capabilities reached `verified` with no run behind them; how many fixes carry a cause. One honest paragraph per design. ⭐ Every input already exists; nothing new is modelled. ⚠️ Counter: it is another report, and this surface has many — it only earns its place if it is delivered where somebody already looks rather than needing to be found.

(b) FOLD IT INTO `where-am-i` AND `loop_status`, which are the two things every session already runs. ⭐ Puts the honest sentence in front of every reader of every design without adding a tool. ⚠️ Counter: `where-am-i` is what a person reads for status, and telling them their evidence is thin on every single session may be exactly right or may be the nag that gets ignored.

(c) MAKE IT PART OF `closure_report`, which already asks whether a design CLOSES against a declared threshold across five legs. A sixth leg — has the evidence ever been confirmed against reality — fits its shape exactly. ⭐ Strongest fit with what exists. ⚠️ Counter: that report already reads `no_closure_criterion_stated` here, so adding a leg to a report nobody has configured may change nothing.

(d) NOTHING, and accept that reflow2 records what it is told. ⚠️ Counter, and it is his: that is defensible for a filing cabinet and not for a thing whose founding claim is that the design tracks what is fielded.

📌 AND THE PART HE ALREADY DOES BY HAND, WORTH NAMING: "We kind of do this aspect of reflow2 all the time when I provide feedback from other reflow2 projects back to this project." That loop — field report → finding → design change — is real, is practised weekly, and its entire transport is ANTHONY COPYING FILES BETWEEN REPOSITORIES. `upstream_status` watches a declared upstream design, so the design-to-design channel exists for versions and not for findings. Whether reflow2 should carry that traffic, or whether a human courier is correct because judgement belongs in the loop, is a separate question this node does not answer.

═══ ⭐ THE "SHOULD IT" HALF IS ANSWERED — ANTHONY, 2026-09-22 ═══

His words: *"Yes, I think a design can say that a design has never closed its loop — if a user designs a house and never comes back and says that it failed an inspection, that is on the user and it is their choice — the design should show that it never completed its loop."*

⭐ AND THE REASONING MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE ANSWER, because it settles the objection that would otherwise have blocked this. Reporting an unclosed loop is NOT reflow2 judging the user's diligence, and it does not cross `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful`. It is the design stating a fact about ITSELF — that no result has ever come back — and leaving the disposition where it belongs. A user who never returns from the inspection has made a choice; the design's job is to make that choice VISIBLE rather than to let silence read as success.

⇒ SO OPTION (d) IS OUT. The remaining question is WHERE it is said — a reading of its own (a), folded into the two calls every session already makes (b), or a sixth leg on the closure report (c) — and that is a delivery question, not a question of whether.

📌 STILL HIS, AND UNANSWERED: which of (a), (b) and (c); and whether reflow2 should carry field-report traffic between designs at all, or whether the human courier is correct because judgement belongs in the loop.

═══ 2026-09-22 (later) — WHERE IT IS SAID IS BUILT, AS OPTION (b) ═══
Step 3 of the ordering Anthony approved folded it into loop_status and where-am-i: req:a-design-says-whether-a-real-result-has-ever-come-back (accepted), cap:the-loop-closure-reading. To make the reading possible he chose, the same day, that a recorded reconcile STAMPS every check it compared (dec:a-reconcile-stamps-every-check-it-compared) — before that an agreeing run left no trace. Never-closed is said in `next` and NOT counted against `clean`, on his reasoning that it is the owner's choice. STILL OPEN on this node: whether reflow2 should carry field-report traffic between designs, or the human courier is correct.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: A design says whether a real test result has ever come back into it
properties.rationale: Recorded as its own question because the other three could all be built and this one would still be unanswered — and it is the one his doubt actually turns on. A design that cannot say whether its own evidence has ever been confirmed against reality cannot support the claim reflow2 is sold on, and the inputs to say it already exist.
